page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the t2d server family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks demonstrate a notable contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng is strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2692.58. However, multi-core CPU performance is weak, scoring 5335.58. Memory bandwidth is generally limited, with read-only large block bandwidth at 35.65 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 22.54 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 25%. Passmark memory scores and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression are poor, placing in the bottom 10%.

For specific workloads, the instance achieves average performance in single-threaded gzip compression (26.13 GB/sec), single-threaded bzip3 decompression (11.31 GB/sec), and Geekbench text processing (1815.0). LLM inference using a small 135M model yields an average text generation speed of 137.32 tokens/sec, though prompt processing is weak at 351.97 tokens/sec. Given these performance characteristics and the lack of local storage, this instance is suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, and single-threaded application tasks rather than memory-intensive or highly parallelized database operations.
